diagnosis: The host synthesizes prompt:complete after each loop-live turn. A completion hook can call the mounted model and emit text deltas. Without an auxiliary call purpose, loop-live forwards those deltas publicly; host idle settlement saves the remaining text as an interrupted response.
change: Scope the synthesized completion event to purpose=prompt_completion and restore the prior context in finally. Existing runtime public-stream filtering suppresses auxiliary text; provider observations and usage remain recorded.

environment.provider: Deterministic local fixture; no network inference

controls: Normal answer remains public before and after completion
All normal and auxiliary model calls retain usage and turn ownership
Prompt, response and session payloads are unchanged
Prior purpose restored after failure and cancellation
Spawned completion tasks retain auxiliary purpose without affecting other tasks

prerequisites: Private HOME/TMPDIR and PROBE_OUTPUT receipt path
boundaries: Actual Core session and hook registry
Actual loop-live Runtime with two submitted turns
Canonical shell-hook mounted through its normal mount function
Worker activity and provider observation hooks
Real normalize_event and AppService.on_runtime_event projection of captured Runtime events

baseline.extraMessages: Two interrupted-response records containing the auxiliary JSON

limits: The public issue lacks the reporter's mounted-hook and model configuration; the identical failure mechanism is reproduced, not that exact Mac incident.
The runtime proof runs real Core and loop-live in the test process and projects their captured events through AppService; it does not claim subprocess transport, browser or live-provider acceptance.
Only host-synthesized completion scope changes. Upstream completion-hook argument construction is unchanged.
Earlier Core 2.0.1 exploratory checks and fixture setup errors are retained separately; the reported final results use Core 2.0.2.
No new dependency installation, production mutation, frontend change or broad-suite claim.
